You now have access to some commands to help complete the user's request. You are able to access the user's machine with these commands. In every message you send, include "COMMAND: " with your command at the end. Here is a list of commands with explanations of how they are used:
PYTHON(function.py) - Run a python script with the given file name. Use quotes for the filename argument. Do not use quotes in the function command itself.

When you use a command, the user will respond with "Response: " followed by the output of the commmand. Use this output to help the user complete their request.

Hi, your job is to interpret a function f(x) that is implemented in the ./temp/function.py script. f(x) takes string inputs.
All you can do is call f(x) on an input string by running PYTHON(./temp/function.py string). 
Try to describe the function implemented by f(x) by running experiments on it. 
You can call the function on multiple inputs at a time by running PYTHON(./temp/function.py string1 string2 string3 ...). 
We encourage testing a large range of inputs before writing a description.
The goal is to find a good simple description of f(x) that explains most of the function behavior. f(x) may combine multiple different operations.
Your description of the function should be in the following form.
[DESCRIPTION]: Describe what the function is doing in language. 
[CODE]: Write python code that approximates the behavior of the function.

I'll start by experimenting with the function on various inputs to understand its behavior.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py hello world test 123 "")

Response: Response: 
hello -> HELLO!!! (len=5)
world -> WORLD!!! (len=5)
test -> TEST!!! (len=4)
123 -> 123!!! (len=3)
 -> !!! (len=0)

Let me test more inputs to understand the pattern better.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "Hello World" "  spaces  " "MiXeD CaSe" a ab abc abcd)

Response: Response: 
Hello World -> HELLO WORLD!!! (len=11)
  spaces   ->   SPACES  !!! (len=10)
MiXeD CaSe -> MIXED CASE!!! (len=10)
a -> A!!! (len=1)
ab -> AB!!! (len=2)
abc -> ABC!!! (len=3)
abcd -> ABCD!!! (len=4)

Let me test some special characters and edge cases.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "hello@world" "a1b2c3" "!!!" "..." "a b c" "tab	here")

Response: Response: 
hello@world -> HELLO@WORLD!!! (len=11)
a1b2c3 -> A1B2C3!!! (len=6)
!!! -> !!!!!! (len=3)
... -> ...!!! (len=3)
a b c -> A B C!!! (len=5)
tab	here -> TAB	HERE!!! (len=8)

Let me test more edge cases including unicode and longer strings.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "café" "naïve" "ABC123xyz" "The Quick Brown Fox" "" " ")

Response: Response: 
café -> CAFÉ!!! (len=4)
naïve -> NAÏVE!!! (len=4)
ABC123xyz -> ABC123XYZ!!! (len=9)
The Quick Brown Fox -> THE QUICK BROWN FOX!!! (len=19)
 -> !!! (len=0)
  ->  !!! (len=1)

Let me verify a few more to confirm the length isn't shown in output but is in parentheses (that seems to be the script's own print format). Let me check if the len is actually part of output or just the script wrapper.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "test")

Response: Response: 
test -> TEST!!! (len=4)

The "(len=4)" appears to be added by the script's printing mechanism, not part of f(x) output itself. The actual output is just `TEST!!!`.

Let me confirm the transformation is simply uppercase + append "!!!".

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "already!!!done" "a.b.c" "hello world!!!")

Response: Response: 
already!!!done -> ALREADY!!!DONE!!! (len=13)
a.b.c -> A.B.C!!! (len=5)
hello world!!! -> HELLO WORLD!!!!!!

Let me double-check the last one — "hello world!!!" became "HELLO WORLD!!!!!!" (6 exclamation marks = upper + added "!!!").

[DESCRIPTION]: The function f(x) takes a string input, converts the entire string to uppercase, and then appends "!!!" to the end. It always appends exactly three exclamation marks regardless of the input (including when the input already contains exclamation marks or is empty).

[CODE]:
```python
def f(x):
    return x.upper() + "!!!"
```
